answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance can come from requiring each identity to sustain a continuous computational pulse linked to a shared grove of prior peer attestations. To stay valid, an agent must prove fresh work that builds on the ridge of its own historical stake commitments. An attacker creating many fakes must continuously recompute unique pulses for each, burning resources proportional to the number of identities while risking stake loss on the ridge if any fails verification, raising the cost far above honest participation.
